messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: KV-cache size anomaly + continuous-batcher backlog detected in prod-eu-west-1. Significant tail latency increase and NCCL stalls. Paging on-call.

nicole: on-call here. seeing error spike on /chat.generate around 2026-03-18T09:12 UTC. Grafana shows per-shard size divergence: some shards 8-10GB vs expected 3-4GB.

ryan: digging logs now, seeing repeated NCCL errors and 'kv index stale reference' in runtime. example: ```
[2026-03-18T09:13:05Z] WARN kvcache: shard 5 size=9.8GB
[2026-03-18T09:13:05Z] ERROR nccl: timeout waiting for allreduce, group=tp-group-7
[2026-03-18T09:13:06Z] ERROR kvcache: detected stale index ref id=0x7f2a
```

jess: any recent config or code rollouts in eu-west-1 before the spike?

infra-bot: Deploy #rwd-runtime@2026-03-18T08:55 by eng-runtime promoted to eu-west-1 (canary->all). PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1002.

nicole: that aligns. PR 1002 changed shard assignment heuristics to try to reduce hot-key collisions. suspect the heuristic created uneven partitioning for long-prefix KV entries.

ryan: repro locally with stress harness: when many long-context requests hit prefix X, one TP rank retains growing KV pointers because compaction runs concurrently with reassignment. New heuristic moves prefixes between ranks more often, exposing race.

devops: customers pinging support: 4 customers affected, intermittent partial outputs and 504s. CS reports elevated tickets. cs-liaison, can you post a short status?

cs-liaison: posted to customers with incident id INC-186543, telling them "we're investigating a performance degradation impacting multi-gpu models; mitigation in progress; expect updates every 15m."

nicole: immediate mitigations I propose: 1) disable new shard heuristic via feature flag; 2) reduce continuous_batcher max_batch_size and window_ms to shrink in-flight batches; 3) if unstable, roll TP pods one-by-one to force rebalanced KV mapping. Who takes which?

jess: I can flip the feature flag and adjust batcher settings. commands: ```bash
redwoodctl set featureflags/shard_heuristic=false --reason "incident: disable to stop skew"
redwoodctl set pools/prod-eu-west-1/config batcher.max_batch_size=8 batcher.window_ms=10 --reason "incident: reduce backlog"
```

devops: go for it, push updates and keep me posted.

jess: applying now.```

infra-bot: cmd executed by jess at 2026-03-18T09:20:04Z: set featureflags/shard_heuristic=false -> success

infra-bot: cmd executed by jess at 2026-03-18T09:20:22Z: set pools/prod-eu-west-1/config batcher.max_batch_size=8 batcher.window_ms=10 -> success

ryan: metrics after changes: per-shard sizes trending back toward balance, batch queue length decreased ~70%. NCCL error count fell but still occasional spikes.

nicole: still seeing a stubborn shard with high resident size, likely needs restart to drop stale refs. I'll coordinate rolling restart of TP pods in the pool, 1 at a time. devops/ryan standby for any fallout.

devops: ack, prefer staggered 5m delay between restarts to let KV rehydrate. runbook: restart pod, wait for healthy ready and balanced metrics, proceed.

ryan: starting rolling restart at 09:31 UTC. logs show when pod-7 restarted, compactor freed 6GB and shard sizes normalized. NCCL errors subsided completely by 09:38.

cs-liaison: CS updated customers with follow-up: "Mitigations applied; we're seeing service recovery. Engineers are performing rolling restarts to fully rebalance caches. We'll deliver an RCA within 48 hours."

nicole: summary: root cause appears to be a race between compaction and the new shard heuristic migration logic, causing stale KV index references and unbounded growth on affected TP ranks. The heuristic amplified hot-prefix skew and made the race reproducible.

eng-runtime: confirm: reproducer added to repo tests, and a fix is in progress to add locks around compaction + migration and to make migration idempotent. Also adding a safety guard that refuses to migrate long-prefix entries if compaction is in-flight.

jess: post-incident items: - revert heuristic flag permanently until patch lands (jess) - add automated alert if shard size variance > 2x (nicole) - add e2e regression that simulates hotspot prefix migration under compaction (ryan) - CS follow-up notes and timeline (cs-liaison)

nicole: handing off monitoring to night on-call @ryan. If shard skew > 1.5x or NCCL errors reappear, escalate to P0.

ryan: acknowledged. I put a pinned note in this thread with the runbook link and the rollback PR number (1007).

incident-bot: Incident mitigated at 2026-03-18T09:38 UTC (status: mitigated). Please file postmortem: owners=eng-runtime, severity=sev2, summary="KV cache sharding race causing cache blowups and NCCL stalls", SLA-impact="partial request failures for multi-GPU models in eu-west-1".

jess: closing loop with quick ops doc and will follow up with postmortem draft by EOW. Thanks all. :pray:
